39 tests ran, 37 pass, and the two failures confirm a real bug in `CSVPrinter`'s constructor contract.

## Summary

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVPrinterAgentTest.java` with 39 self-contained JUnit 4 tests covering construction/validation, `print`/`printRecord`/`printRecords` (including the `ResultSet` overload and error paths), all four `Quote` policies, escaping-only formats, comments, `println`, `close`/`flush` delegation, and custom delimiters.

Two tests fail, both exposing the same bug in `CSVPrinter`:

- **`testConstructorInconsistentFormatThrowsIllegalArgumentExceptionPerJavadoc`** and **`testConstructorQuoteNoneWithoutEscapeThrowsIllegalArgumentExceptionPerJavadoc`** — `CSVPrinter`'s constructor Javadoc states it throws `IllegalArgumentException` "if the parameters of the format are inconsistent" (e.g., quote char equal to delimiter, or `Quote.NONE` with no escape character set). In practice, the constructor calls `format.validate()`, which throws `IllegalStateException` instead. Since `IllegalStateException` is not an `IllegalArgumentException`, callers coding to the documented contract (catching `IllegalArgumentException`) will not catch this exception — a real mismatch between documented and actual behavior.

All other 37 tests pass, confirming the rest of `CSVPrinter`'s behavior (null handling, quoting/escaping rules, comment formatting, resource delegation, etc.) matches its documented contract.
